Add an organization level to a plan's grain

Source: R/regrain.R
regrain.Rd

Inserts a new grain column name, before the column before, whose value on each row is read from another grain column through groups: for instance a funnel column grouping channel into Brand and Performance. Every value of from in the plan must sit in exactly one group; anything else is refused, naming the values.

Usage

regrain(plan, name, from, groups, before = from)

Arguments

plan

A MediaPlan, without subplans.

name

The new column's name, such as "funnel". Not a column the plan already has, nor one the package reserves.

from

The line item column the new one is read from, such as "channel".

groups

A named list: each group's name, and the values of from in it – list(Brand = c("TV", "Streaming"), Performance = "Search"). A group may name values the plan does not have.

before

The line item column the new one goes in front of; by default from, since a grouping is coarser than what it groups and the grain is ordered coarsest-first.

Value

The same plan (same @id) with name in its grain and data.

Details

Line item keys change – line_item() gains the new column – and nothing else does: the rows, their spend, and the plan's @id, @parent_id, @status, @approved_on, @rationale and every other slot are carried as revise() carries them. A target that names the old columns selects the same rows after, so a stored op still replays. A stored add or allocation names every grain column, so it gains the new one too, and the plan's @edits replay on a parent regrained with the same groups.

To regrain a set of revisions and drafts, regrain each plan with the same arguments: the ids, and so lineage() and current_approved(), are unchanged.

A plan holding subplans is refused: a subplan's grain must contain its parent's, so the column would have to be added beneath it too.

See also

assign_sections(), which needs every organization level to be a grain column.

Examples

plan <- media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(week = as.Date("2026-07-06"),
             channel = c("TV", "Streaming", "Search"),
             planned_spend = c(50, 30, 40)),
  grain = "channel", time = "week", name = "Q3"
)
by_funnel <- regrain(plan, "funnel", from = "channel",
                     groups = list(Brand = c("TV", "Streaming"),
                                   Performance = "Search"))
by_funnel@grain
#> [1] "funnel"  "channel" "week"   
line_item(by_funnel@data, line_item_grain(by_funnel))
#> [1] "Brand | TV"           "Brand | Streaming"    "Performance | Search"
